claim_ceiling: Independent Preisach-style rate-independent relay memory; demonstrates physical input-history dependence and return-point memory, not learning, intelligence, agency, or biological life

source.classical_model: Preisach-style ensemble of independent bistable hysterons with upper/lower switching thresholds

physical_background.citation: Du, Behera & Vaikuntanathan, Physical Considerations in Memory and Information Storage, Annual Review of Physical Chemistry 76 (2025), 471–495
physical_background.relevance: Reviews information storage/retrieval through energetics, dynamics, statistical mechanics, Hopfield models and physical realizations.

physical_background.citation: Generalizing multiple memories from a single drive: The hysteron latch, Science Advances (2025-01-29)
physical_background.relevance: Demonstrates return-point memory in hysteron systems and richer sequence memory with frustrated interactions; the OLI v0 control uses independent hysterons only.

physical_background.citation: Mörée & Leijon, Review of Hysteresis Models for Magnetic Materials, Energies 16(9), 3908 (2023)
physical_background.relevance: Distinguishes history-dependent Preisach-type models from simpler direction-dependent Duhem-type models and from rate-dependent dynamic hysteresis.

model.state_space: finite collection of bistable hysteron states
model.reset: drive below the minimum lower threshold

benchmark_cases.interpretation: Current input alone is insufficient; the relay state carries physical input history.

benchmark_cases.expected: The hysteron-state vector at the second visit to 0.75 must equal the vector at the first visit to 0.75.
benchmark_cases.interpretation: A nested minor loop returns to the same state when the prior extremum is revisited.
Opposite saturation erases the prior relay configuration for this finite ensemble.

benchmark_cases.expected: Both monotone paths reach identical relay state at the same final drive, independent of the number of intermediate dwell samples.
benchmark_cases.interpretation: This relay model is rate-independent; do not confuse with dynamic hysteresis generated by frequency-dependent lag.

benchmark_cases.expected: Both cycles have identical outputs; thresholds and weights are unchanged.
benchmark_cases.interpretation: Repeatable physical memory does not imply task learning or parameter adaptation.

metrics.positive_weight_fraction: sum of weights in positive state / total weight
metrics.same_input_history_separation: absolute difference in magnetization after two histories at identical current input
metrics.return_point_state_error: Hamming distance between relay states at repeated turning point
metrics.rate_independence_state_error: Hamming distance between coarse/fine monotone protocol final states
metrics.threshold_drift: maximum absolute threshold change across cycles
metrics.loop_area: not currently emitted by the Rust module; compute from the externally recorded input-output trace in benchmark analysis

anti_leakage: All samples from one ensemble and initial state belong to one trajectory.
Do not count repeated input points within one history as independent physical specimens.
Split benchmark cases by threshold ensembles, not by points from the same drive sequence.
Keep independent-hysteron and interacting-hysteron systems as separate mechanism families.
